name: heerich
category: A4. Vector, typography, diagrams and stills
role: JavaScript voxel scene engine with SVG output
notes: 2026-11-15: Triage reason: Assess Node/server-side route, API stability and deterministic output. Revisit after a stable API or repeat workflow.
2026-11-15: Legacy schema value used for a listed-only candidate; this is not evidence of PRD inclusion.
2026-11-24: Toolkit guide written from examples/heerich-voxel-svg (Node oblique SVG, 27 polygons); untested areas marked in the guide.

evidence.result: 3x3x3 union minus one corner voxel, oblique SVG: 54 raw faces, 27 polygons in 3 face names (9 each), 0 paths; two runs byte-identical; Node v22.19.0
evidence.scope: In Node, 3x3x3 cube minus one voxel renders to oblique SVG with 27 polygons; reruns byte-identical; heerich 0.21.0, Node 22.19.0, macOS arm64. No occlusion, perspective or GPU.

summary: Small JavaScript engine for defining voxel scenes, boolean geometry operations and SVG rendering from oblique or perspective cameras. Its vector output suits compact isometric illustrations; the API and server-side determinism need a scoped check.
use_when: Generate compact voxel scenes and SVG views from JavaScript
Use boolean voxel operations for small isometric illustrations
avoid_when: Use Three.js for interactive 3D scenes, animation or broad model support
Use Blender when a full 3D editor and offline renderer are required

assessment.rationale: Official repository describes a zero-dependency JavaScript voxel-to-SVG engine with boolean operations and camera projections. A stable Node API and release cadence remain unconfirmed.
